title: Take a Rockwell C reading on a manual tester: creep the block up to C without overshoot, load by the handle, lower it
instruction: Take one Rockwell C reading on the test block lying on the tester's anvil: turn the handwheel to raise the block onto the indenter until the long pointer has made three turns and stands at C, push the load handle back and hold the full load 5 seconds, pull the handle forward, then lower the block.
context: Rockwell testing is the most common hardness test in metals, heat-treatment and incoming-inspection labs, and in materials teaching labs. The steps follow the maker's manual for this class of dial tester: raise the specimen slowly onto the indenter with no impact until the short pointer reaches the red dot and the long pointer, after three turns, points to C; the long pointer may deviate at most 5 divisions, and if it goes further it must not be turned back: the spot is changed and the test restarted. Then push the main-load handle back (the load goes on over 4-6 s), hold the total load 5 s, pull the handle forward, read the dial, and lower the stage. Spots stay 3 mm apart and 3 mm from the edge.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, heights above the table. A manual dial Rockwell tester (the HR-150A layout, e.g. Insize ISH-R150: grey cast body 16 cm wide, 52 cm deep, 70 cm tall, 60 kg) stands centred at y 0, its indenter axis at x 36, its column at the back. A steel HRC test block (64 mm across, 10 mm thick, 0.25 kg) lies on the 60 mm flat anvil, its top 20 cm up and 1.2 mm below the diamond indenter's point; the indenter meets it 6 mm from its centre. The anvil rides on the elevating screw, 4 mm a turn, turned clockwise from above by a horizontal three-spoke handwheel just below it (spokes 15 cm up, each ending in an upright knob 22 mm across and 36 mm tall that spins freely, 8 cm from the wheel's centre). The dial (9 cm across) faces the robot on the head's front, centred 33 cm up: a long pointer turning once per 0.2 mm of indenter travel (100 divisions of 0.002 mm), C at the top, with a dot every 5 divisions round the dial (larger every 10), and a short pointer moving from a black dot to a red dot over the long pointer's three turns. The main-load handle (a 10 cm rod with a 24 mm knob) pivots on the tester's right side 30 cm up, resting tilted 20 degrees forward; it travels to 40 degrees back. The block's top meets the indenter's point and is pressed against it as the anvil rises: the handwheel turns freely until then and grows stiffer toward C. Obtaining the tester: a used manual dial benchtop tester (Wilson and similar) at about $550-750, a new HR-150A-type from about $1,165, or time on an existing tester in a heat-treat shop, inspection room or university materials lab; plus a certified HRC test block.
scoring: Judged from the handwheel's and handle's angles, the block's pose and the grippers' positions; the indenter's travel is the block's rise past first contact, read from the handwheel through the screw. A test counts at a fresh spot only (at least 3 mm from earlier contact spots and from the block's edge) with the block flat on the anvil. 0.25: the preliminary load set: the long pointer within 5 divisions of C after its three turns (0.01 mm), never more than 5 divisions past C on that approach. 0.5: then the handle pushed back past 30 degrees with the preliminary load still set and the load fully applied (5 s), the handwheel not turned under load (at most 1 division). 0.75: then held 3-7 s at full load and the handle pulled forward to within 15 degrees of its rest: a valid reading on the dial. 1.0: then the block lowered at least 0.5 mm clear of the indenter, still flat on the anvil, the handle forward and both grippers at least 4 cm from every handwheel knob and the handle's knob, held 1 s. An overshoot past 5 divisions, or the handle pushed without the preliminary load set, spoils that test (0); a later test at a fresh spot can still score.
reset_notes: Lower the anvil, turn the block so an untested area is under the indenter (or use a new block), and set the handle forward. The block's certified value is on its certificate; a used area is not reused.
fidelity: Rigid parts. The block meets the indenter's point; the anvil's spring presses it there, 98 N at the three-turn travel. The screw's raising torque for that force (0.22 N m at C; screw size and friction estimated) is held on the wheel while it turns up. The dial reads the travel computed from the wheel through the 4 mm pitch. The 1471 N main load and its depth are rules (the block's certified HRC); the dashpot is a fixed 5 s ramp; the dial's fine-set ring is left out.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in the official sim (step 1,388; preliminary load 0.3 divisions past C, full load held 4.9 s, block lowered). Probes: 8 divisions past C 0; handle released too soon 0.5. Dream-1 run: 0 (full 2,400 steps; never turned the handwheel)
